(2) 'pin the connector that actually reports connected, never an assumed one' DISCHARGED -- exactly one connector connected (HDMI-A-1), discovered not hardcoded. ROOT CAUSE OF THE FALSE PREMISE, AND IT IS A FABRICATION: US-552's bash fixture declared `# The panel's advertised mode list as a 3.5" 480x320 HDMI panel reports it: PANEL_MODES='...480x320'`. Nobody had read the EDID. The fixture ASSERTED the hardware fact that made the pin look applicable, so the suite could only ever go green -- same shape as the latched magnetometer and IAT-as-ambient. Secondary cause is a UNIT CONFLATION: docs/hardware-reference.md 'Resolution | 480 x 320 pixels' is the GLASS, and the script consumes it as a KMS SIGNAL TIMING. The OSOYOO HDMI35 is a SCALER panel -- 480x320 glass behind a chip that takes standard HDMI timings and downsamples in hardware. A native mode was never on offer.

WHAT I CHANGED (test-only, deliberately disposition-independent -- the target mode is Atlas's call and I did not pre-empt it): relabelled PANEL_MODES as the SYNTHETIC write-path fixture it actually is; added OSOYOO_HDMI35_MEASURED_MODES with the command+date it was measured; added Scenario 15 pinning that the REAL panel makes the script refuse without touching the boot cmdline (catalog 50 -> 56 assertions). Scenario 15 encodes NO ruling on what to pin instead, so it survives whichever way BL-034 goes.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE PIN: the Pi is not failing to reach native -- there IS no native mode, and the panel has been hardware-downscaling all along. A 34px driver-must-read value lands on the 320px glass at roughly 13-15 physical px (0.444 stretched / 0.375 letterboxed; I measured the signal, not the glass, so both are given). That is about HALF the F-127 floor, and it is a better explanation of the marginal arm's-length reads than anything in F-132. US-560's AC-5 was right to be suspicious of the scale.

RECOMMENDATION IN BL-034 (Atlas to rule, do NOT force): pin 720x480. It is the ONLY advertised mode matching the glass's 3:2 aspect (480/320 = 720/480 = 1.5), giving a uniform 0.667 scale, ~23px for a 34px value -- ~1.5-1.8x better than today with zero aspect distortion, NO code change and NO forcing (ECLIPSE_DISPLAY_MODE=720x480). Forcing 480x320 with a D-suffix modeline bypasses EDID and can scan out black in a car with no local recovery; that is exactly what interlock 3 exists to stop.

stories.completionNotes:
passes:true. All four of Atlas's section-3 defects enumerated and dispositioned below, per AC-3 (which explicitly forbids fixing one and closing the story). Three FIXED, one DOCUMENTED AS AN HONEST BOUND with cause.

=== 3a THRESHOLD MISCALIBRATED / FALSE 'healthy' -- FIXED, and this is the load-bearing change. ===
The AC forbids a re-tuned constant and asks for a discriminator that actually separates the states. Shipped: PRESENCE + DWELL. Healthy was MEASURED as exactly zero post-restart, so zero is the BOUNDARY of the band, not a point inside it -- which means presence needs no tuned magnitude at all and cannot be mis-calibrated against a rate nobody has measured yet. Any marker at all => the failure class is live; sustained CONTINUOUSLY for a 60s dwell (two 30s timer ticks) => wedged. This is threshold+dwell, the same shape Spool arrived at independently for the coolant fan-cycle ceiling, and the story's own AC names that parallel.
  - `errorCount <= 0` is now the ONLY route to REASON_HEALTHY.
  - New REASON_WEDGE_SUSPECTED for markers-present-but-not-yet-sustained: NOT a restart, and pointedly NOT 'healthy'. Its log line says 'is NOT healthy ... Healthy is measured ZERO; this is not zero.'
  - New `wedged` flag on the decision/outcome is True on wedge_detected AND on cooldown AND on budget_exhausted -- declining to act is not a claim that the display is well.
  - The dwell rests on a marker-presence clock persisted in the ledger. It requires UNBROKEN presence (never-flap rule 7): one measured-zero tick clears it, so an isolated GL complaint cannot combine with another minutes later to fake a sustained wedge. An unreadable journal leaves it UNTOUCHED -- absence of evidence must not forgive an accruing wedge.
  - `DEFAULT_ERROR_THRESHOLD` is GONE as a verdict. The number 100 survives as `DEFAULT_MARKER_READ_CAP`, which is what it always genuinely needed to be: an I/O bound stopping an uncapped read pulling megabytes per tick off a Pi the wedge has already pegged. A STRUCTURAL test asserts the read cap cannot re-enter decideAction -- behaviour alone cannot pin that, because a re-tuned constant (10 instead of 100) would pass every behavioural test while re-creating the defect at the next regime shift.
  - Gate: 84 and 101 (the two counts Atlas logged one tick apart) are asserted to produce the SAME verdict as each other; and a 5-tick replay of one continuous freeze at the real observed counts asserts REASON_HEALTHY appears zero times while a restart still eventually fires.

=== 3b `journalctl --grep` exit-1 MISREAD AS UNREADABLE -- FIXED, and the premise was re-measured live rather than inherited. ===
`--grep` exits 1 when NOTHING MATCHED, which on a healthy kiosk is every tick, so US-523 reported a clean kiosk as an honest-unknown -- the exact inverse of its own docstring, and it left a genuinely broken journal indistinguishable from a working one. Fix MEASURES readability instead of inferring it from an exit code: on any non-zero exit with EMPTY stdout, a new `journalIsReadable()` probe runs one unfiltered `journalctl --lines=1`; probe OK => the zero is real (return 0), probe fails => still None. Deliberately unfiltered (no -u, no --grep) because the question is 'does the journal read at all', which a unit-scoped probe would answer wrongly for a unit with no entries. Costs nothing on a healthy tick -- the probe only runs on the failure path, pinned by a test. Non-empty stdout with a non-zero exit stays None (a partial/aborted read is not a measured zero).
  VERIFIED ON THE REAL PI 2026-08-21, both halves: the grep returns RC=1 with empty stdout on zero matches, and the unfiltered probe returns RC=0. Honest bound: I ran both over ssh as mcornelison, not inside the unit's cgroup/SupplementaryGroups=systemd-journal, so I measured the exit-code behaviour, not the unit's exact journal scope.

=== 3c ~3 MINUTE DETECTION LAG -- NOT FIXED. Deferred with cause, documented as an honest bound in the module header. ===
The markers are a LAGGING indicator by construction: they appear when an allocation is finally attempted, not when painting stops (froze ~16:15, burst 16:18:32). NOTHING inside this watchdog can close that -- it would need a signal that LEADS rather than lags, i.e. a repaint heartbeat published BY the page, which is a dashboard change and a different story. Rather than leave the claim floating, the module header now states the bound explicitly: this watchdog CANNOT claim 'detected within 60s of the freeze'; it detects within ~a dwell of the MARKERS, and the markers may trail the freeze by minutes. The timer header carried exactly that false claim ('a wedge is seen within about one window and recovered inside ~1.5 min') and has been corrected in place.
  NOTE, and it is a genuine improvement rather than a consolation: detection got EARLIER anyway. Atlas measured 1 marker at 16:16:39 and dismissed it as 'not the known class' -- under presence+dwell that same sample STARTS the clock, so the restart lands ~50s sooner than the count-based path managed. Presence is observable long before a count reaches 100.

=== 3d RESTART BUDGET EXHAUSTS IN ~18 MIN -- policy UNCHANGED (Atlas called it 'correct policy'); OBSERVABILITY fixed per AC-5. ===
The defect the AC actually names is that 2 of 5 restarts were consumed mid-drive and went unsurfaced. Fixed: the budget is now stated on EVERY tick as 'N of M restarts this hour (K left)' -- including routine healthy ticks -- rather than only in the single WARNING emitted at the instant of a restart. A tick with any consumed budget logs at WARNING instead of INFO, because a display that has already self-healed this hour is not a routine tick; a tick with an untouched budget stays INFO, so the WARNING keeps its information content (both directions pinned). The ceiling also rides on the outcome object (`maxRestartsPerHour`), since '2 restarts' is not observable and '2 of 5' is. The ledger on tmpfs carries the attempts, so `cat /run/eclipse-kiosk-watchdog/ledger.json` shows the spend too.
  NOT DONE, and flagged rather than silently skipped: surfacing the budget ON THE PANEL. That needs a state file under /run/eclipse-obd/states/, and this unit must NEVER declare RuntimeDirectory=eclipse-obd -- systemd would DELETE that directory (including the live states/ the emitters write) when the oneshot exits. That foot-gun is documented in the unit header and is a real constraint, not an excuse; panel surfacing is a separate story with a different owner for the write path.

=== OTHER ===
AC-4 resolution-INDEPENDENT: held. Nothing here reads or assumes a display mode, so US-560's refuted premise / BL-034 does not touch it.
THREE PINS MOVED, NOT DELETED (each repointed docstring says what it used to assert and why the move is the deliverable): 'counts 0/1/99 are all healthy' -> only measured zero is; 'at-or-above-100 restarts' -> dwell-driven restart; 'any non-zero journalctl exit is unreadable' -> exit 1 with a readable journal is a clean zero. Deleting them would have erased the record of what changed.
Ledger seam widened from readHistoryFn/writeHistoryFn to readLedgerFn/writeLedgerFn over a LedgerState (attempts + presence clock) -- one file, one write. A pre-US-561 ledger reads as attempts + no clock, so the single tick that straddles a deploy keeps its restart budget (pinned). A junk presence clock is discarded rather than coerced: JSON `true` would float() to 1.0 and read as a 56-year dwell, restarting the panel on the next single marker (the US-517 trap, pinned over 4 junk shapes).
New fail-safe: markers present + ledger unwritable => REASON_LEDGER_UNWRITABLE (exit 2), never 'healthy'. The dwell lives in the ledger, so a detector that has lost its memory must not issue a clean bill of health -- that is the same false-healthy this story removes, arriving by a different road.
FULL-SUITE REGRESSION NOT RUN IN-LOOP per TD-059. Scope was src/pi/display/kiosk_watchdog.py + its gate + two deploy unit-file comment blocks; I ran tests/pi/display/ AND tests/deploy/test_kiosk_watchdog_install.py (the US-540-b scoped-gate lesson) and grepped tests/ for every renamed symbol -- zero stale references outside the structural guard. No src/ module outside kiosk_watchdog.py imports it (verified by grep), so PM-time full-suite risk is low.
VALIDATION STILL OWED (validationCriteria #1, hardware): 'wedge the display deliberately and watch the verdict across several ticks'. That needs the code deployed to the Pi and a deliberately wedged kiosk; it is not closable from this harness and I did not claim it. The 5-tick replay test reproduces the observed counts in software, which is evidence about the discriminator, NOT about the live box.

passes:true. All 5 acceptance criteria dispositioned below. The headline is that I RE-MEASURED THE PREMISE ON THE LIVE PI instead of inheriting it, and the measurement NARROWED the defect to something more specific -- and more dangerous -- than the story text describes.

=== WHAT I MEASURED, AND HOW IT CHANGED THE DIAGNOSIS ===
AC-1 asserts 'eclipse-powerwatch emits ZERO application log lines today'. That is FALSE as written, and I checked before building to it. The journal on chi-eclipse-01 holds plenty of application lines from this unit -- 'powerwatch: GPIO6 PLD => external power LOST', 'powerwatch: PLD power-loss 68s into boot-grace (120s) -- ignoring', UpsMonitor I2C retry warnings -- all from the same pids. What it holds ZERO of, across 8 service starts, is the arm-success line.
The true mechanism: **this module never configured logging at all.** With no root handler, Python falls back to `logging.lastResort` (level WARNING, stderr, bare message). So the arm-SUCCESS line, which is `logger.info`, was discarded on the floor every single time; the arm-FAILURE line, which is `logger.error`, would have printed fine -- it has simply never fired. AC-1 is right that both calls are unconditional on their branches; a code reviewer reading lines 439-456 would find nothing wrong, because the defect is in what is NOT there.
**Why that distinction matters rather than being pedantry:** silence on this service meant EITHER 'armed fine' OR 'the instrument is broken', and nothing could tell them apart. That is the same false-healthy shape US-561 removed from the kiosk watchdog one story earlier in this same sprint. Had I built to the story text I would have gone looking for missing log calls and found none.

=== AC DISPOSITIONS ===
(1) 'emits zero application log lines, both unconditional' -- PREMISE CORRECTED ON EVIDENCE, defect CONFIRMED and localised. Both calls verified unconditional; the arm-success line verified absent from 8 starts; WARNING+ verified present. Root cause identified as missing logging configuration, not a missing call.
(2) 'emit the arm decision unconditionally: armed / not-armed, with cause on the failure branch' -- MET. New `emitArmDecision()` fires on BOTH branches with no input that logs nothing. The failure branch keeps every fact the old ERROR carried (pinned by a parametrised MOVED-pin test over all 6 of them: REFUSING to arm / OBD collector / NOTHING will be powered off / pi.powerWatch.pldGpioPin / pldPowerPresentHigh / redeploy) and adds the measured evidence. Both branches carry one `ARM_DECISION_PREFIX`, so a single grep answers the operator's question: `journalctl -u eclipse-powerwatch.service --grep='ARM DECISION'`.
(3) 'PREREQUISITE FOR THE HARDWARE INVESTIGATION' -- MET, and this drove the message design. The CIO must be able to separate 'safety never armed' from 'safety armed and the hold-up path failed'. A bare verdict cannot do that, so each line states what was MEASURED -- pin, line readability, and the actual power-present reading -- which further separates 'wrong pin/polarity' from 'line unreadable'. Pinned by test on both branches.
(4) 'OBSERVABILITY ONLY' -- HELD. No GPIO6 ownership change, no hold-up-path change, no change to the arm DECISION itself (`provider.startupArmCheck()` is untouched), no change to the armed path's runtime behaviour beyond one extra startup read for the evidence. The only control-flow change is on the disarmed branch, which previously did nothing but block forever.
(5) ruff/lint clean -- MET on all 3 touched files.

=== THREE FIXES, AND WHY THE FIRST ONE ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN ENOUGH ===
1. `main()` now calls `setupLogging()` from the config's logging.level, BEFORE anything reports a decision. This is the root-cause fix and it un-silences the whole INFO tier -- including this service's own 'powerwatch sync: companion service disabled -- no-op' line, a silent hole on the shutdown path that nobody had noticed either. Level only, deliberately NO logFile: this service is shutdown-critical and must not open a second writer on the OBD app's log file. Its stdout IS the journal, and StreamHandler flushes per record so block-buffering cannot strand a line.
2. The arm decision is emitted at WARNING (armed) / ERROR (not-armed), NOT INFO. **Deliberate, and I want it on the record as a decision rather than an accident.** It fires exactly once per service start, so severity costs no journal volume, and this module already uses WARNING for once-per-event operational facts (the power-loss trigger). The point is defence in depth: pinning a safety fact to a tier that a config change can silence is precisely how it went missing. If `LOG_LEVEL` is ever set to WARNING, or logging configuration regresses to lastResort again, the arm decision still gets through. Pinned as a FLOOR (`levelno >= WARNING`) with the reasoning in the test docstring, plus a both-directions test that armed and not-armed keep their distinct levels.
3. The disarmed hold re-states its cause every `DISARMED_RESTATE_SEC`. Pre-US-566 the failure branch announced once and then sat on a bare `threading.Event().wait()` forever -- `systemctl is-active` reports `active` either way, so a disarmed Pi looked exactly like a protected one, and the one line explaining why would age out of the journal. Declining to arm is not a claim that the shutdown path is well.

=== A SMALL SSOT LEAK FIXED INSIDE THE LINES I WAS REWRITING ===
The old ERROR read its diagnostics from the raw `pld.*` (`pld.isAvailable`, `pld.isExternalPowerPresent()`) while the decision itself came from `provider.startupArmCheck()`. That is two acquisition sites for one fact -- the one place the explanation could disagree with the decision it explains. Evidence now reads through the PowerSourceProvider SSOT. Not scope creep: it is the exact expression I was replacing, and it is the project's standing design directive.

=== ON TDD HONESTY ===
The unit tests would have gone red pre-change only in the trivial ImportError way (the functions did not exist), which the progress log rightly calls 'one useless red'. So the load-bearing guard is in the systemd-parity subprocess -- the only test that exercises the real `main()` wiring -- and I verified it is NOT vacuous rather than assuming it: a scratch probe confirmed that with no handlers installed, lastResort emits a BARE message (no level name, no logger name) and drops INFO entirely. Both new parity assertions ('logger name present' => a configured handler, not lastResort; '| INFO' present => the level filter admits INFO) were therefore genuinely red before this change, and they agree with the live Pi journal independently.

=== VALIDATION CRITERIA -- ONE DISCHARGED, ONE OWED AT DEPLOY ===
#2 ('force the failure branch -> ERROR line with cause, not silence') -- DISCHARGED IN-LOOP. Covered behaviourally (unconditional emit, ERROR level, cause + evidence + all 6 preserved remediation facts) and the re-statement loop is covered with a bounded waitFn.
#1 ('boot the Pi and read the powerwatch journal -> an explicit arm decision line appears') -- **OWED AT DEPLOY, NOT CLOSABLE FROM THIS HARNESS, AND I DID NOT CLAIM IT.** It needs this code deployed and the Pi rebooted, and deploy is PM's. **PM: after deploying V0.29.30, run `journalctl -u eclipse-powerwatch.service --grep='ARM DECISION' --no-pager` -- exactly one line per boot, and it should read ARMED. If it reads NOT-ARMED, that is the finding the CIO's X1209 hold-up investigation has been missing.** I measured the BEFORE state only (zero lines).

=== FULL-SUITE STATE FOR PM'S INTEGRATION GATE ===
tests/pi/power/power_watch -> 71 passed, exit 0, zero pre-existing reds in this scope. Full `pytest tests/` NOT run in-loop per TD-059. Risk is low but NOT zero and here is the honest bound: `setupLogging()` sets the ROOT logger level and CLEARS existing root handlers, so any third-party INFO in this process's import graph now reaches the journal too. In steady state that graph is quiet (smbus2 has no logging; urllib3/SyncClient only run inside a shutdown window; UpsMonitor's own lines are already WARNING), so I expect roughly one extra startup line -- but it is a behaviour change to a shutdown-critical service and worth a glance at journal volume on the first deploy. `src/pi/main.py` already runs the whole OBD app at INFO, so this is consistent with project practice rather than novel.

passes:true. All 7 acceptance criteria dispositioned below.

=== THE HEADLINE: THIS STORY IS EVIDENCED ON REAL HARDWARE, NOT ON A FIXTURE THAT ASSERTS HARDWARE ===
The gate's entire design rests on ONE empirical claim -- that a real sensor dithers, so N consecutive BIT-IDENTICAL samples cannot occur naturally. Every test that feeds the gate values chosen BY the test proves the mechanism and proves NOTHING about the ICM-20948. That gap is exactly what refuted US-560 earlier in THIS SPRINT: US-552's fabricated PANEL_MODES fixture asserted the hardware fact that made its own suite unfalsifiable (BL-034).
So I pulled 90 s of genuinely captured parked-car samples off chi-eclipse-01's edr_imu_sample and committed them as tests/fixtures/imu_stationary_90s_2026-08-21.csv. ONE capture proves BOTH directions, which is what makes it evidence rather than illustration: on the SAME rows, through the SAME gate, accel and gyro are never refused (1821 and 1845 distinct values respectively) while the magnetometer IS (1 distinct value across 1845 samples). A gate that fired on nothing would pass the first half; a gate that fired on everything would pass the second; only a working discriminator passes both.
The fixture is SELF-VERIFYING: test_capture_matchesItsDocumentedProvenance re-derives the row count and the per-channel distinct counts FROM THE DATA and asserts they match the CSV's own header. Regenerating it rounded, truncated or synthetic goes red THERE, loudly, instead of silently weakening every assertion built on it. The prose header and the bytes cannot drift apart unnoticed.
A missing fixture is a FAILURE, deliberately not a skip. A skip would quietly restore the unfalsifiable state this test exists to end -- and it would do it while the suite still read green.
The pre-existing synthetic +/-1-ULP test is KEPT but RENAMED and RELABELLED (test_check_syntheticUlpDither_neverStale). Its docstring claimed 'REAL stationary-vehicle behaviour' while feeding math.nextafter output, which never repeats BY CONSTRUCTION -- so it could not have failed even if the chip were latched. It is a legitimate BOUNDARY pin (one representable float step is still a difference, so the check cannot be loosened into a tolerance comparison) and it now says so instead of overclaiming.

=== AC DISPOSITIONS ===
(1) ONE STORY, NOT THREE -- MET. One module (plausibility_gate.py) owns the MECHANISM; each reader declares its own PHYSICS via ChannelPolicy. All three symptoms route through it.
(2) BIT-IDENTITY, NOT LOW VARIANCE -- MET, and it is the load-bearing choice. Samples are compared as packed IEEE-754 bytes, NOT with `==`: 0.0 == -0.0 is True (an equality test would call a channel latched across a real sign-bit transition) and NaN != NaN (which would hide a genuinely stuck garbage read). No magic threshold exists anywhere in the module. Proven on real data: the accel channel repeats 24 values across the window and still never trips, because the check requires a CONSECUTIVE run.
(3) EXISTING FAILED-POLL PATH -- MET. A refused critical channel raises GatedReadingError, which lands in pollOnce's existing failure handler: nothing published, seq still advances, consumer sees the same honest gap an I/O fault produces. No second silence mechanism to keep honest.
(4) sensor_mute / sensor_stale DISTINCT FROM sensor_absent -- MET. Absent means 'not wired'; these mean 'wired, enumerated, answering -- and not measuring'. Check 1 runs FIRST and its verdict is final for the sample, so a run of zeros stays sensor_mute rather than being re-labelled 'stale' once it has repeated enough -- the two reasons name different faults and must not blur.
(5) DERIVED FIELDS GO TYPED-NA WITH THEIR INPUT -- MET. _CHANNEL_DERIVED_FIELDS writes the rule down once: mag -> headingDeg, gyro -> pitchDeg/gradePct. Applied LAST in buildImuState so a gated source always beats a computed value -- the caller may still hold a perfectly derivable number from a channel just proven not to be measuring, and the arithmetic working is not evidence that the input was real. A gated mag also DROPS the held reading outright, so the pairing window cannot carry it into one last heading with a fresh timestamp on it. Accel is deliberately absent from that map: it is the gravity reference under ALL derived fields, so its refusal blanks the whole instrument and writes immediately, bypassing the display cadence exactly as an unplug does.
(6) syncPending ON BOTH LAYERS -- MET. The emitter emits None (was a hardcoded 0) AND syncTile renders an em-dash (was `s.pending == null ? 0`). passes:true. THE STORY'S OWN PREMISE IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, and that is the headline. US-565 states 'the lever is CNTL2 but the correct setting is unknown'. CNTL2 is not the lever at all.

=== WHAT I MEASURED, AND WHY IT CHANGED THE FIX ===
I re-measured the premise on the live Pi rather than inheriting it: 20,000 rows over 16 minutes, mag_x/y/z 1 distinct EACH while accel_x showed 93 and gyro_z 1357. Latch confirmed, current, on the running deployment.
Then the characterization the story demanded. Three findings, in the order they arrived:
  (1) CNTL2 ALREADY READ BACK 0x08 -- continuous 100 Hz -- BEFORE any change. The chip was already in the mode the story assumed was wrong.
  (2) A VERIFIED write of 10 Hz (transfer finished, readback 0x02) changed the latch NOT AT ALL. Atlas's earlier rate sweep (100Hz->zeros, 10Hz->latched, 50Hz->partial) was reading NOISE: those writes went through slave4, and slave4 does not complete once the cyclic slave0 readout is running -- so most of them never reached the chip. MY OWN FIRST RUN HAD THE SAME DEFECT and I caught it only because I printed the readback: every CNTL2 read said 'transfer did not finish', which meant the writes on that same path had not landed either. I rebuilt the probe to quiesce slave0 and VERIFY every write before believing any trial. A probe that cannot fail is not a measurement.
  (3) THE DECISIVE ONE: polled directly over slave4 with the shadow quiesced, the AK09916 was CONVERTING AND DITHERING -- raw X took 6 distinct values across 11 passes with ST1.DRDY set -- while dev.magnetic sat frozen. The chip was healthy the entire time.
So the fault is the ICM-20948's cyclic slave0 shadow readout: it performs ONE transfer and then stops. Over a 12 s window mag changed exactly once, at sample index 1, then held for 270 more samples while accel changed 265 times on the same die. Tracking WHERE the changes fall, not just how many, is what made that visible -- a distinct count of 2 cannot tell 'updated at init then froze' from 'updating slowly'.

=== THE FIX ===
Disable the aux master, set INT_PIN_CFG.BYPASS_EN, read the AK09916 as its own I2C device at 0x0C on the primary bus. Accel and gyro still come from the ICM at 0x69 and bypass does not affect them -- the fix is provably confined to the one broken channel, which matters because Atlas measured accel and gyro as HEALTHY.
MEASURED ON THE SHIPPING CODE PATH against the real chip: 350 distinct 3-vectors in 500 stationary samples, longest bit-identical run 2, against the gate's run limit of 100. Before: 1 distinct in 20,000.

=== AC DISPOSITIONS ===
(1) SEPARATE from US-564 -- MET. Not one line of the gate was touched; this is a device-layer fix at the device seam. ImuReader still reads a handle with .acceleration/.gyro/.magnetic exactly as before.
(2) NOT A GUESSED CONFIG VALUE -- MET, and it is the AC I took hardest. Every number in the fix has a measurement behind it, the probe that produced them is committed and re-runnable (offices/ralph/scripts/characterize_magnetometer.py), and the characterization DISPROVED the lever the story named rather than confirming it. Had I 'just set 50 Hz and declared victory' as Atlas warned, the suite would have gone green and the channel would still be dead.
(3) N DISTINCT, NOT 'IT CHANGED ONCE' -- MET IN SOFTWARE, and note the fix's own failure mode was literally 'it changed once': the broken path changes exactly one time before freezing, so 'it changed' would have scored the DEFECT as a pass. Acceptance is asserted as distinct counts AND longest-identical-run against the gate's dwell, on real captured data. SEE THE OWED VALIDATION BELOW for the rotation half.
(4) DO NOT USE THE BROKEN GETTER -- MET. Ak09916Direct.readMode() reads CNTL2 as a register. Verified on hardware: the shipping code read 0x08 directly and matched the configured mode. The broken getter is never called anywhere in the fix.
(5) headingDeg renders NA via US-564's gate until this lands -- ALREADY DISCHARGED by US-564 before I started; nothing owed. It now publishes real bearings again, which is what TD-087 is about.
(6) ruff/lint clean -- MET on all 4 touched Python files.

=== VALIDATION CRITERIA -- ONE DISCHARGED, ONE OWED, AND I DID NOT CLAIM IT ===
#2 (read the data-rate register directly, not the broken getter) -- DISCHARGED ON HARDWARE with the shipping code, not the probe.
#1 (ROTATE the vehicle/board through a full turn) -- **OWED, HARDWARE, NOT CLOSABLE FROM THIS HARNESS.** I cannot rotate the board over ssh. What I CAN say is strictly stronger than 'it changed once' and strictly weaker than the rotation: STATIONARY on the bench the channel produces 350 distinct 3-vectors in 500 samples with a longest identical run of 2. Stationary is the HARD case for this direction -- there is no motion to force variation, so everything surviving is genuine sensor dither. A rotation will produce far more; it remains owed as the acceptance the story actually wrote. **PM/CIO: rotate the board through a full turn after deploy and confirm the bearing sweeps.**

=== THE PIN THAT MATTERS MOST, AND WHY IT IS BOTH STRUCTURAL AND BEHAVIOURAL ===
The burst read runs ST1..ST2 INCLUSIVE (9 bytes) because reaching ST2 is what releases the AK09916's data latch and permits the next conversion to land. A 'tidier' 6-byte data-only read from HXL looks more efficient and SILENTLY re-creates the original defect -- the values stay plausible, they just stop changing. So the test fake MODELS THE CHIP'S LATCH RULE: it only loads a new measurement once a read has reached ST2. I verified the falsifiability rather than assuming it -- through the same fake, the shipped 9-byte frame yields 8 distinct of 8 and a 6-byte HXL read yields 1 of 8. A fake that always served fresh data would have scored the broken driver and the fixed one identically.

=== CONFIG IS VERIFIED BY READBACK, NEVER ASSUMED ===
configure() reads WHO_AM_I and refuses an unidentified device (bypass exposes a NEW address on the primary bus; decoding whatever answers there into micro-teslas is how you publish a fabricated heading), then transits through power-down per the datasheet and READS CNTL2 BACK, raising if it does not match. That is the exact defect class this story closes: the adafruit driver writes CNTL2, DISCARDS the transfer-completion flag its own helper returns, and never reads back -- so a mode that never reached the chip was indistinguishable from one that did, for months.

=== A MAG FAULT MUST NOT COST ACCEL AND GYRO, AND THAT CLAIM IS TESTED ===
The degrade path is EXTRACTED from the hardware-only glue into _attachDirectMagnetometer so it is reachable by test (parametrised over config error / OSError / ValueError). A claim that exists only as a try/except inside a '# pragma: no cover' function is a claim nothing enforces -- the inert-guard anti-pattern. On failure the bare ICM comes back, so gMag/pitch/grade/g-trail keep flowing and the latched mag that returns with it is refused by US-564's gate as sensor_stale rather than published.

=== TWO REAL CAPTURES, ONE GATE, OPPOSITE VERDICTS ===
The new 90 s bypass capture is replayed through the US-564 gate and is NEVER called stale; the ORIGINAL latched capture through the SAME gate configuration IS. Without that second half the first test would be satisfied by a gate that refuses nothing at all. The fixture is self-verifying -- a test re-derives its row count and per-channel distinct counts FROM THE DATA and asserts they match its own header, so regenerating it rounded or synthetic goes red there rather than silently weakening everything built on it. A missing fixture ASSERTS rather than skips.

=== FILED, NOT SILENTLY WORKED AROUND ===
TD-087: headingDeg is a REAL reading now but UNCALIBRATED -- measured |B| ~90 uT against Earth's ~52 uT at this latitude, i.e. a hard-iron offset comparable to the field itself, which can swing a bearing by tens of degrees. The card prints it to 0.1 deg, a precision claim the measurement cannot support. Calibration is explicitly out of scope per conditionalOutcomes -- but it is no longer BLOCKED, and that transition should not be silent.
I-us565: three shared-surface facts go stale on deploy and all three are outside my write access -- specs/architecture.md 10.8 (0x0C is now an occupied address; design-gate DoD, PM Rule 10), MEMORY.md's 'COMPASS IS FABRICATED / Fix = US-565' entry (re-scope, do NOT delete -- the drives-<=41 caveat stays true), and the upstream library report Atlas asked for, now with the larger slave0 finding attached.

passes:true. All 5 acceptance criteria dispositioned below. Two things I MEASURED changed what this story is: one refutes a warning the sprint has been carrying, the other found a real bound hiding inside AC-2's word "structural".

=== FINDING 1 -- THE 1280x720 FLAG IS REFUTED. PM/IRIS/ATLAS PLEASE READ BEFORE US-556/US-557. ===
The US-560 iteration flagged, and my own agent note repeated, that "the chromium kiosk runs with no --window-size and no --force-device-scale-factor, so the dashboard renders into a 1280x720 CSS-pixel viewport, while US-557's band budget is ~320-canvas arithmetic -- budgeted against one canvas, rendered on another". I re-measured instead of inheriting it, and THE CONCLUSION DOES NOT FOLLOW. The observation was true (there is no window-size flag) but the inference was wrong.
US-482 authors the whole UI inside `#stage`, a FIXED `width: 480px; height: 320px` box grown by `transform: scale(var(--scale, 1))`, with carousel.js setting `--scale = Math.min(innerW/480, innerH/320)`. Both sides agree (CSS `#stage` and JS `STAGE_W`/`STAGE_H`), and the existing tests/ui/test_carousel_letterbox_scale.py already pins it. A CSS transform scales the RENDERED output; it does not change the layout box. So the viewport size only moves `--scale` -- the CSS layout canvas is 480x320 whether the panel scans out 480x320, 720x480 or 1280x720.
CONSEQUENCES, and they are the useful part: (a) US-557's band budget in ~320 CSS px IS the correct arithmetic and does NOT need re-doing against 720p; (b) settling BL-034 to a different mode CANNOT silently invalidate US-555/556/557, because none of them is measured against the panel mode -- it only changes `--scale`, i.e. how big the same layout paints; (c) the flag should be STOOD DOWN rather than carried into 556/557. I have not deleted it from the agent note as a fact -- I have replaced it with this measurement.
WHAT REMAINS TRUE FROM BL-034, and it is a different claim: a 34px value on 320px of glass still lands at roughly 13-15 PHYSICAL px. That is a legibility question about the panel's downscaling, and it is real. It is NOT a layout-arithmetic question, and conflating the two is what produced the flag. I measured the layout canvas, not the glass.

=== FINDING 2 -- `1fr` IS `minmax(auto, 1fr)`, SO AC-2's "STRUCTURAL" HAS A BOUND. ===
AC-2 says the clock stays centred "regardless of version-string length (structural, not auto-margin)", and the design note says the drift is "structurally impossible rather than merely avoided". That is ALMOST right and the gap matters. A `1fr` track is `minmax(auto, 1fr)`: its minimum is its content's min-content size. So the two side tracks are equal -- and the centre track therefore centred -- only while each cluster FITS its share of the free space. A cluster that outgrows its share pushes its track past 1fr and the clock moves.
I did not paper over this and I did not silently deviate from the spec: I shipped AC-1's literal `1fr auto 1fr` and MEASURED the bound. Computed from the shipped values only -- token sizes, the bar's own padding and gap, the kebab's --tap-min floor, nothing copied out of the design note -- the guaranteed side-track share is 168.8px against a left cluster of 107.4 and a right cluster of 127.2. Both fit with room. The bound is now a test, so the day someone adds a fifth glyph or a long version string it goes RED with the actual numbers instead of the clock quietly sliding.
THE ONE-LINE VERSION FOR IRIS: the grid does make the drift impossible for the CONTENT WE SHIP, which is what the story wanted; "unconditionally" would need `minmax(0, 1fr)`, and that trades drift for overflow -- a worse failure on a 480px bar. AC-1 states the defect as "40px box + 34px glyph inside a 28px bar". US-557 moved the bar to 34px one story earlier in THIS sprint (the prior close note flagged the 28 as stale and told me to re-read it). Re-read against 34, the two halves come apart:

(2) STAMP ON ITS OWN LINE, COUNTS TO #sys-detail -- MET; see the next section, because this is where the story actually was.
(3) ONE 12-HOUR RULE -- MET. Extracted `fmtTimeOfDay(d, withSeconds)`; `fmtClock` now delegates and holds no arithmetic of its own. Guarded by a COUNT (`h % 12 || 12` appears exactly once in the whole file, comments stripped so prose quoting the rule cannot inflate it) PLUS a delegation check -- the count alone could be satisfied by deleting `fmtClock` outright. A third test pins that the top bar still shows NO seconds: the extraction grew a seconds field for the stamp, and leaking it into `fmtClock` would change a shipped surface this story never asked to touch.
(4) UNPARSEABLE -> RAW, NEVER 1970/NaN -- MET, and STRICTER than the AC in a way that matters. `new Date` is far too willing: it reads "412" as the year 412 and a ZONELESS ISO string as LOCAL. Neither is an Invalid Date, so both would sail past a literal isNaN check and put a confident wrong date on the tile -- and the zoneless case would land silently hours off, re-creating the exact contradiction this story exists to remove. So only a zone-qualified ISO-8601 instant is formatted; everything else is echoed verbatim. Parametrised over 7 inputs including the raw string the tile used to print.
(5) null -> `never` -- MET, unchanged, plus the missing-key case (`undefined == null` in JS) because a Pi/dashboard deploy skew is a state this project has actually been in.
